grammar.title: 一般时与进行时
rows: 一般时描述习惯或完整事件；be + -ing 描述某时正在进行的动作。
I usually walk to work, but today I am taking the bus.
我通常走路上班，但今天坐公交车。
grammar.tip: 过去背景动作可用 was/were doing；持续到现在的活动可用 have/has been doing。
grammar.say: I usually walk to work, but today I am taking the bus.

grammar.title: 动态动词与状态动词
rows: know / believe / want 等状态动词通常不用进行时；think 等可因含义改变用法。
I think this is useful. I am thinking about a new goal.
我认为这有用。我正在考虑一个新目标。
grammar.tip: think 表认为时用一般时；表示思考过程时可用进行时。
grammar.say: I think this is useful. I am thinking about a new goal.

writingTask.title: 评论面试建议
writingTask.task: 写 80–120 词，回应阅读中的建议。表明赞同或保留意见，并给出个人例子。
writingTask.focus: 用 I agree that / However / For example 支持观点。
starters: I agree that examples are useful because ...
writingTask.model:
I agree that an example is more useful than a list of qualities. In my first interview, I said I was responsible, but I did not explain why. Later, I described how I organized a group project and checked everyone's tasks. That answer felt clearer.

However, I also think candidates need time to choose a suitable example. Being nervous does not mean someone is unqualified. Practicing with a friend can help. Next time, I will prepare two short stories and ask about the training available.

readings.book: 第4册 1.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Show what you can do
readings.text:
At a practice interview, Nora described herself as creative and responsible. The interviewer asked for an example, and Nora paused. She had listed qualities but had not explained how she used them.

Next time, she described a community event. When the printer broke, she made signs by hand and asked a friend to check the details. The event started on time. This story showed creativity and responsibility without a long list of adjectives.

An interview is also a chance to learn about the workplace. Nora now prepares two questions about training and teamwork. She wants to find a job where she can learn, not simply give impressive answers.
readings.zh:
在模拟面试中，诺拉说自己有创意、负责任。面试官要她举例，她却停顿了。她列出了品质，却没说明如何运用。

下次她讲了一次社区活动：打印机坏了，她手工制作标牌，并请朋友核对细节。活动准时开始。这个故事体现了创造力和责任心。

面试也是了解工作环境的机会。诺拉现在会准备有关培训和团队合作的问题。她想找到能学习的工作，而不只是给出漂亮的回答。

qs.q: Why did Nora pause?
opts: She had not prepared an example.
qs.a: She had not prepared an example.
qs.why: 她只列了品质，没有解释具体的做事经历。

qs.q: How did she make the signs?
qs.why: 文章明确说 made signs by hand。

qs.q: What does she ask about now?
qs.why: 结尾提到准备培训和团队合作的问题。

writingTask.title: 饮食调查报告
writingTask.task: 用给出的二十人数据写 80–120 词的报告，包含发现、建议和样本限制。
writingTask.focus: 用 most / half / a quarter 描述比例，不把小样本推广到所有人。
checklist: 使用至少两种数量表达
writingTask.model:
We asked twenty classmates about their lunch habits. Most usually brought lunch from home. A quarter usually bought it near college, and three students used both options equally often.

Half sometimes wasted food, usually because they bought too much. Six said they would try smaller portions. These results suggest that offering different portion sizes could be useful.

The survey is small, so we cannot assume that everyone has the same habits. We recommend a short trial at the café, followed by a second survey to find out whether less food is wasted.

readings.title: Lunch habits in our class
readings.text:
We asked twenty classmates about lunch. Twelve usually brought food from home, five bought lunch near college, and three did both equally often. Most said price was important, but several also mentioned packaging.

Half of the group sometimes threw away food. The most common reason was buying more than they could eat. Six students said they would try smaller portions if the café offered them.

These results describe one small class, not everyone in the city. Still, they suggest a practical experiment. For one week, the café could offer two portion sizes and ask customers which they prefer. After it collects the answers, it can decide whether to continue.
readings.zh:
我们询问了二十位同学的午餐习惯。十二人通常带饭，五人在学校附近买午餐，三人两种方式同样频繁。大多数人重视价格，也有几人提到包装。

一半人有时会扔掉食物，最常见原因是买得太多。六人表示，如果咖啡馆提供小份餐，他们愿意尝试。

结果只代表一个小班级，不能代表全市居民。不过，咖啡馆可以试行一周大小两种份量，再根据顾客反馈决定是否继续。

grammar.title: too 与 enough
rows: too + 形容词；形容词 + enough；enough + 名词。
The bag is too small. It is not large enough. I have enough money.
包太小了。它不够大。我有足够的钱。

grammar.title: 修饰比较级
rows: much / far / a lot 表大差异；a little / slightly 表小差异；nearly / almost 可修饰 as ... as。

writingTask.title: 产品评价
writingTask.task: 用 80–120 词评价一件日常用品，说明优点、不足和适合的人群。
writingTask.focus: 使用比较级及 too/enough，具体评价尺寸、质量或使用体验。
writingTask.model:
I bought this small backpack for my daily commute. It is much lighter than my old bag and large enough for a notebook, lunch, and a water bottle. The handle feels strong, and the pockets are easy to reach.

However, the main pocket is too narrow for my larger laptop. I should have checked the measurements more carefully. The bag is good value for someone who carries only a few things. If you need space for a large computer, I would suggest trying a bigger model before you buy.

readings.title: A bargain that was not cheap
readings.text:
Leo bought a used desk online because it cost much less than a new one. The photo looked clear, and the seller said it was in good condition. Leo forgot to ask for the measurements.

When the desk arrived, it was too wide for his doorway. Taking it apart required a tool he did not have. A neighbor helped, but the job took the whole afternoon. Delivery and a replacement screw added to the cost.

The desk now works well, and Leo is pleased with its strong surface. However, he no longer judges value by the price alone. Next time, he will check the size, the delivery cost, and the time needed to assemble an item before paying.

readings.title: A neighborhood voice
readings.text:
A small bakery wanted to reach new customers without losing its neighborhood character. Instead of hiring a celebrity, the owner invited three regular customers to describe their favorite bread. Each agreed to appear in a short video.

The designer who made the logo kept the familiar blue door in the picture. The video showed where the bread was made and named the people who prepared it. As a result, viewers could connect the products with real faces.

More people visited the bakery that week, but the owner did not claim that the video caused every visit. A street festival was happening nearby too. She decided to ask new customers how they had heard about the shop before paying for another advertisement.

readings.book: 第4册 5.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: An apology with a plan
readings.text:
A repair shop promised to return Nora's bicycle on Friday. When she arrived, the work had not been finished. No one had called her. She needed the bicycle for the weekend and was upset.

The manager first said that the shop had been busy. This explanation did not solve Nora's problem. He then apologized clearly, acknowledged the missed promise, and offered a loan bicycle at no extra charge. Nora accepted it.

On Monday, the manager sent a message confirming that the repair was complete. He also explained a new reminder system for delayed orders. Nora still disliked the delay, but she appreciated the practical response. An apology cannot change the past; it can explain what will happen next.

经理先说店里太忙了，但这没解决问题。他随后明确道歉，承认没履行承诺，并免费提供一辆临时代步车。诺拉接受了。

周一，经理确认维修完成，也说明了延误订单的新提醒机制。诺拉仍不喜欢延误，但认可实际补救。道歉不能改变过去，却可以说明接下来怎么办。

grammar.title: 现在与过去的被动语态
rows: am/is/are 或 was/were + 过去分词；by 可引出动作执行者。
Books are donated every week. The shelves were built last month.
每周都有人捐书。书架是上个月建的。
grammar.tip: 被动强调动作承受者；不清楚或不重要的执行者可省略。
grammar.say: Books are donated every week. The shelves were built last month.

grammar.title: 情态动词的被动形式
rows: can / should / must 等 + be + 过去分词。
The forms must be signed. Old chairs can be repaired.
表格必须签字。旧椅子可以修理。
grammar.tip: 不能漏掉 be；这里的 can 表示可能或能力，must 表要求。
grammar.say: The forms must be signed. Old chairs can be repaired.

writingTask.title: 社区项目报告
writingTask.task: 用 80–120 词介绍图书交换项目，包含事实、参与者引语和改进建议。
writingTask.focus: 用准确引语支持观点；用被动语态描述项目实施。
writingTask.model:
A book exchange was created in the community room. The shelves were built from donated wood, and twelve families provided the first books. People can borrow a book and bring another later.

The project has encouraged conversation. One volunteer said, 'I met neighbors I had never spoken to before.' The lower shelf also makes it easier for children to choose books.

Some damaged books were donated, so clear guidelines have been added. I suggest using large, bilingual labels next. These could help more residents find suitable books and feel welcome in the space.

readings.title: A shelf for everyone
readings.text:
Residents turned an unused corner of their community room into a book exchange. The shelves were built from donated wood, and the first books were collected from twelve families. Visitors can take a book and bring another when they are ready.

The project is small, but it brings people together. One volunteer said, 'I met neighbors I had never spoken to before.' A parent explained that the lower shelf helped young children choose books by themselves.

Some books arrived damaged, so the organizers added clear donation guidelines. Books should be clean and complete. They also plan to label sections in two languages. The next review will ask whether more residents can find books they enjoy.
readings.zh:
居民把社区活动室一个闲置角落改成了图书交换区。书架用捐来的木料制作，第一批书来自十二个家庭。访客可以拿走一本书，方便时再带来另一本。

一位志愿者说：“我认识了以前从没说过话的邻居。”一位家长说，低书架方便孩子自己选书。

由于一些捐来的书已损坏，组织者增加了要求：书应干净完整。他们还计划增加双语分类标签，并评估更多居民能否找到喜欢的书。

readings.title: One message, two meanings
readings.text:
When Wei sent a short reply saying 'Fine,' Maya thought he was annoyed. Wei was actually boarding a bus and had little time to type. Later, he explained that he had meant to agree with her plan.

Written messages do not always carry the tone we hear in speech. An emoji may help friends, but its meaning is not universal. Different groups use the same symbol in different ways. In a formal email, a complete sentence is often clearer than a symbol.

Wei now adds a little context when he is in a hurry: 'That works for me. I'll reply properly this evening.' Maya asks for clarification instead of guessing. Both have learned that a quick question can prevent a long misunderstanding.
readings.zh:
魏只回复了一个“好”，玛雅以为他生气了。其实他正在上公交车，没有时间打字。后来他解释，他的意思是赞同计划。

书面信息不一定传达口语中的语气。表情符号可能帮助朋友交流，但含义并不统一。正式邮件中，完整句子往往比一个符号更清楚。

现在魏忙时会补一点背景：“我觉得可以。今晚再详细回复。”玛雅则会询问，而不是猜测。他们认识到，简短的确认能避免长时间的误会。

rows: if + 过去式，主句 would/could + 原形：想象与现在不同的情况。

writingTask.title: 回应两种观点
writingTask.task: 写 80–120 词回应阅读中两人的意见，提出适合你自己的做法。
writingTask.focus: 明确引用别人观点，再给自己的理由和折中建议。
writingTask.model:
Maya argues that fewer notifications can help people concentrate, and I agree. I often lose my place in a book when messages appear. However, I also agree with Wei that family calls should remain available.

For my own routine, I would silence work messages for one hour in the evening and keep calls on. I would tell my coworkers when I planned to reply. If I had an urgent shift, I would change the plan. I wish I had tried this during my last course, but a short experiment now could still help.

readings.book: 第4册 8.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Connected, but not all day
readings.text:
In a practice podcast, Maya said that turning off notifications helped her concentrate. She checked messages twice during her study session instead of reacting to every sound. Wei disagreed with switching a phone off completely because his family might need to call.

They found a compromise. Work messages could wait during planned downtime, while calls from family could still come through. Both agreed to tell people when to expect a reply.

Their plan was an experiment, not a rule for every job. Some workers must respond quickly during a shift. Maya and Wei decided to test their routine for one week, record how they felt, and adjust it if it created new problems.
readings.zh:
在一段练习播客中，玛雅说关闭通知有助于集中注意力。学习时她只检查两次消息，而不是每听到提示音就回应。魏不同意完全关机，因为家人可能需要来电。

他们找到了折中办法：在计划的休息时间里，工作消息可以等，家人来电仍能接通。他们也会告知别人何时能回复。

这只是实验，并不是适用于所有工作的规则。有些人值班时必须迅速回应。两人决定试行一周，记录感受，必要时调整。

readings.title: A doorway for more people
readings.text:
The neighborhood arts center had a wide front door, but three steps made it difficult for some visitors to enter. A resident using a wheelchair asked whether another entrance was available. Staff showed her a side door, but it was often locked.

At a community meeting, residents explained that an entrance should be easy to find and use. The center installed a ramp and added clear signs. Staff also checked that the route stayed free of boxes.

The changes helped wheelchair users, parents with strollers, and visitors carrying equipment. The manager invited feedback instead of assuming the work was finished. Making a public space welcoming is an ongoing task, and the people who use it can identify problems that others miss.

writingTask.title: 比较发明的影响
writingTask.task: 写 80–120 词比较阅读中两种工具，解释它们对你的价值。
writingTask.focus: 用 similarly / whereas / unlike 表示相同或不同；至少使用一句过去假设。
starters: If I had ..., I might have ...
writingTask.model:
Like Leo, I value the bicycle because it gives me independence. I can travel short distances without waiting for a bus. Similarly, a phone reminder helps me manage my own time. Both tools reduce my dependence on other people.

However, their effects are different. A bicycle changes how I move, whereas a reminder changes how I remember plans. Last month, I forgot a library appointment. If I had set a reminder, I might have remembered to go. I would not call one tool the greatest invention, because each solves a different problem in my life.

readings.title: A small tool, a different outcome
readings.text:
During a discussion about useful inventions, Leo chose the bicycle. He said it had given him a way to travel independently before he could drive. Maya chose the alarm clock because it helped her organize early shifts.

Wei thought about a less obvious tool: the simple reminder on his phone. Once, he had missed a meeting because he wrote the date in a notebook and forgot to check it. If he had set a reminder, he might have arrived on time.

The group did not agree on one greatest invention. Instead, they noticed that value depends on the problem someone needs to solve. A tool does not have to be complicated to make a difference, but people still need to use it thoughtfully.

魏想到了手机提醒功能。他曾把会议日期记在本子里，却忘了查看，因而错过会议。如果设了提醒，他可能会准时到达。

大家没选出唯一“最伟大”的发明，而是意识到价值取决于需要解决的问题。工具不必复杂也能有作用，但仍需要人合理使用。

grammar.title: remember / forget / stop 后接 -ing 或 to do
rows: remember doing 是记得做过；remember to do 是记得要做；stop doing 停止某动作；stop to do 停下去做另一事。

我记得见过她。记得给她打电话。我们停止说话来听。
grammar.tip: forget doing 涉及过去经历；forget to do 表忘了完成任务。根据含义选结构。

writingTask.title: 有论据的回应
writingTask.task: 写 80–120 词回应课堂录播提议，提出你的立场、理由及一个限制。
writingTask.focus: 用 First / In addition / However / Therefore 连接论证。
writingTask.model:
I support recording short explanations with the professor's permission. First, students can replay a difficult point instead of trying to remember every word. This could help students who combine work and college. In addition, written notes would offer another way to review.

However, a recording cannot replace every part of learning. Students still need opportunities to ask questions and discuss ideas. I would keep the small-group sessions in person. Therefore, I support the class's mixed approach, followed by a review at the end of the semester. We should judge the plan by whether it helps students learn.

readings.book: 第4册 11.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Technology with a purpose
readings.text:
Some students want every lecture recorded, while others worry that recordings will make people stop attending. In a class discussion, Nora suggested asking what problem the recordings would solve.

A student who worked evening shifts said she sometimes needed to review difficult explanations. Another student said that small-group discussions could not be replaced by watching a video. Both had reasonable points.

The class proposed recording short explanations, with the professor's permission, while keeping discussion sessions in person. They also requested written notes for students who preferred reading. The plan did not treat technology as either perfect or useless. It gave different tools different purposes and included a review at the end of the semester.
readings.zh:
一些学生希望录下每节课，另一些担心录播会让人不来上课。诺拉建议先明确录播要解决什么问题。

一位上晚班的学生有时需要重听难懂的讲解，另一位认为视频无法替代小组讨论。两人都有合理观点。

全班提议征得教授许可后录制简短讲解，讨论课仍面对面进行，并为偏好阅读的人提供文字笔记。这项方案既不把技术看成完美，也不视为无用，而是让不同工具承担不同用途，并在学期末评估。

grammar.title: 强调结构
rows: What + 从句 + be ...；The thing (that) ... + be ...，突出特定信息。
What I remember is the smell of fresh bread. The thing I loved was the garden.
我记得的是新鲜面包的香味。我喜欢的是花园。
grammar.tip: 先确定想强调的部分，再选择清晰的句式；注意主谓一致。
grammar.say: What I remember is the smell of fresh bread. The thing I loved was the garden.

grammar.title: 替代与指代
rows: one/ones 替代可数名词；do/does/did 替代已提及动作；so 替代已说过的情况。
I like the blue one. She remembers it, and I do too. I think so.
我喜欢蓝色那个。她记得，我也记得。我想是的。
grammar.tip: 代词和替代词必须有清楚的所指；不可数名词通常不用 one 替代。

writingTask.title: 总结与回应
writingTask.task: 写 80–120 词，先准确总结两种观点，再给出自己的回应。
writingTask.focus: 用 although / whereas / however 连接不同观点，区分总结与个人看法。
checklist: 区分原文与自己的意见
writingTask.model:
Maya emphasizes the companionship that a pet can provide, whereas Wei focuses on the responsibility involved. Although their experiences differ, both agree that appearance alone is not a good reason to choose an animal. Owners need to consider long-term care.

In my view, both points matter. A pet can become part of meaningful family memories, but affection does not replace daily care. Before making a decision, a household should discuss time, space, and who will help when someone is away. I liked the example of helping a neighbor because it shows another way to spend time with animals.

readings.book: 第4册 12.4 目标对应原创材料
readings.title: Remembering a family pet
readings.text:
In a discussion about pets, Maya described the dog she had grown up with. What she remembered most was its excitement when she came home. Caring for it had taught her to keep a routine.

Wei enjoyed that story, but he pointed out that a pet also needs time, space, and reliable care. His family had decided not to get a dog when everyone was away during the day. Instead, they sometimes helped a neighbor walk hers.

The speakers agreed that animals should not be chosen only because they look cute. Maya valued the companionship, whereas Wei emphasized responsibility. Their different experiences led to a shared conclusion: before getting a pet, consider what you can provide throughout its life, not just how you feel today.
readings.zh:
讨论宠物时，玛雅描述了从小陪她长大的狗。她最难忘的是回家时它兴奋的样子。照顾它教会了她遵守规律。

魏喜欢这个故事，但指出宠物需要时间、空间和可靠照料。他家白天没人，便决定不养狗，而是偶尔帮邻居遛狗。

两人都认为，不能只因动物可爱就养它。玛雅重视陪伴，魏强调责任。他们最终一致认为：养宠物前应考虑能否长期照料，而不只是今天的心情。
